policy_point: AI must be beneficial for humanity
statement: Our core philosophy dictates that any AI interaction should intrinsically benefit humanity as a whole.
details:
- Requires long-term societal audits prior to scaling
- Demands public metric disclosures regarding system alignment
- Prohibits deployment of models where harms statistically outweigh net social goods
- Includes regular check-ins with international human rights watchdogs
- Ensures open-source or academic variants are released for public evaluation

policy_point: Avoid creating or reinforcing unfair bias
statement: Datasets and models must be sanitized against explicit and implicit demographic biases.
details:
- Regular monitoring against demographic discrepancies during inference
- Implementation of active bias-bounty programs for generative endpoints
- Formalizing fairness testing across diverse global demographics
- Enforcing structural reviews of early dataset collection
- Ensuring model failures do not disproportionately affect minority profiles

policy_point: Be built and tested for safety
statement: Defensive red-teaming and security-first development is strictly mandated.
details:
- Mandatory adversarial training iterations applied to language and image models
- Sandbox testing against real-world biological threat scenarios
- Implementation of stringent input sanitization protocols
- Deployment of dedicated anomaly detection during real-time inference
- Establishing isolated 'kill switches' for misbehaving cloud systems

statement: A formal board holds full operational veto power over controversial deployments.
details:
- All board members undergo ethical training based on international law
- The board retains final authority to suspend API endpoint generation
- Includes rotating seats for independent 3rd-party researchers
- Meets biweekly to audit anomalous AI reports from internal researchers
- Maintains an open internal dialogue with transparent feedback loops

impact: Restricted certain use cases across commercial platforms
statement: Rigorous controls apply to the extraction and identification of human biometric facial data.
details:
- Banned all open-source release of generalized facial identification systems
- Heavily restricted enterprise API usage to verified, audited partners
- Mandated explicit user opt-in for algorithmic facial categorization
- Instituted immediate data deletion policies on biometric caches
- Funded external privacy advocacy research surrounding public surveillance

policy_point: Enhanced external collaboration on AI ethics
statement: Cooperation with global governance establishes realistic cross-border AI safety caps.
details:
- Organized multiple industry-wide AI safety summits with international leaders
- Funded standardizing non-profit organizations operating in alignment
- Established open communication channels with competing AI innovators
- Jointly published standard metrics for LLM evaluation benchmarks
- Partnered with educational institutions to share safety research globally

impact: Clear path for AI responsibility and alignment
statement: Strategic multi-year governance plans dictate long-term responsible scaling.
details:
- Standard definitions applied universally across all regional branches
- Embedded responsible AI directors directly onto core architectural teams
- Integrated ethical impact scoring directly into developer CI/CD pipelines
- Shifted corporate OKRs to explicitly reward safety constraint adherence
- Built a multi-year timeline tracking alignment progress transparently

impact: Provided exhaustive model cards directly on product endpoints
statement: Full disclosure regarding model capacities, training sets, and weaknesses is non-negotiable.
details:
- Deployed detailed interactive Model Cards attached to all consumer APIs
- Released public datasets outlining exactly which materials are constrained
- Expanded open-source interpretability research grants
- Mandated real-time watermarking for generated images and text
- Allowed independent researchers deep-access to model weights for auditing

policy_point: Generative AI copyright and intellectual property shields
impact: Provided legal indemnification for generative outputs
statement: Protections are extended to users against intellectual property friction arising from model utilization.
details:
- Instituted a two-pronged IP indemnity policy covering training and outputs
- Automatically filtered core models against literal copyrighted memorization
- Funded artist-opt-out architectures for visual model scraping
- Enforced strict prompt guidelines regarding copyrighted character synthesis
- Established a dedicated legal review committee for commercial AI enterprise clients

impact: Capped autonomous capabilities in production environments
statement: Systems utilizing multi-agent recursive behaviors must adhere to strict temporal and resource limits.
details:
- Enforced hard loop-cutoffs preventing infinite recursive agentic behavior
- Banned out-of-bounds internet traversal without explicit human oversight
- Implemented real-time token constraints on autonomous web interactions
- Established deep-state parameter monitoring for complex agentic plans
- Required user confirmation dialogs before agentic execution of financial or destructive actions

impact: Preemptive policies guarding against post-quantum security vulnerabilities
statement: Advanced models interfacing with quantum architectural accelerators require specialized encryption layers.
details:
- Restricted hybrid model query generation to classified or enterprise sandboxes
- Deployed post-quantum lattice cryptography on all model endpoint caches
- Mandatory oversight by global oversight committees for threshold intelligence tiers
- Disabled autonomous compilation of security-bypassing executables natively
- Ensured transparent logging of algorithmic actions to dedicated audit pipelines
